expiresIn.other: This code works for {count} more seconds, for one iPhone.

clipboard.soundHint: The phone goes quiet while mirroring.

clipboard.iphoneSoundHint: Off: the sound stays on the iPhone. On: it plays here instead. Over a cable, macOS then shows its microphone indicator while you mirror, because it counts the iPhone's sound as a microphone; this Mac's own microphone is never used. Turn this off, or click Sound on this Mac while mirroring, to turn the indicator off.

updates.title: Updates
updates.checkHint: Once a day, {app} looks at its releases page and tells you when a new version is ready to download.

installer.noTeams: No Apple ID in Xcode yet. Follow the steps below, or use a provisioning profile.
installer.freeTeam: Free team: the app stops opening after 7 days. Install it again then.
installer.paidTeam: Paid team: the app keeps working for a year.
installer.noPhones: Connect the iPhone with a cable, unlock it, and tap Trust if it asks.
installer.busy: {message}. This takes a minute or two.
installer.trustTitle: One more step on the iPhone
installer.trust1: Open Settings, General, VPN & Device Management.
installer.trust2: Tap the developer named after your Apple ID, then Trust.
installer.opened: FreeFlect is open on the iPhone.
installer.reinstallBy: With a free team, install it again before {date}.
installer.expired: It has stopped opening. Install it again.
installer.missingProject: The iPhone app project is missing. In a development copy, run xcodegen in native/ios/MirrorCompanion.
installer.noProfiles: No provisioning profiles are installed on this Mac. Follow the steps below, or use an Apple ID.

help.teamTitle: How to add an Apple ID
help.team2: Click + at the bottom, choose Apple ID and sign in. A free Apple ID works.
help.team3: Your Apple ID now shows a team, such as "Your Name (Personal Team)".
help.team4: Come back here and press Refresh, then choose that team.
help.teamNote: With a free Apple ID the app stops opening after 7 days and has to be installed again. A paid Apple Developer membership makes it last a year.
help.profileTitle: How to use a provisioning profile
help.profile1: Sign in at developer.apple.com, then Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles. This needs a paid Apple Developer membership.
help.profile2: Under Identifiers, create the App IDs com.freeflect.ios, com.freeflect.ios.broadcast and com.freeflect.ios.share, or one wildcard App ID such as com.freeflect.* or com.yourname.*.
help.profile3: Under Devices, add this iPhone's identifier (UDID). Xcode's Devices window shows it.
help.profile4: Under Profiles, create an iOS App Development profile (or Ad Hoc) for that App ID, with your certificate and this iPhone. Download it and double-click it.
help.profile5: Make sure the matching certificate is in your keychain, then press Refresh and choose the profile.
help.profileNote: A profile someone gave you works too, if it includes this iPhone and you have its certificate. The app lasts as long as the profile.

brands.xiaomiSecurityWhy: Lets taps and typing reach the phone. Xiaomi asks you to sign in to a Mi account for this.
brands.installViaUsbWhy: Lets you drop APK files to install them.
brands.permissionMonitoringWhy: Needed on some models for taps to work.
brands.chargeOnly: Allow ADB debugging in charge only mode
brands.chargeOnlyWhy: Keeps the connection when USB is set to charging.

platform.title: Which phone do you want to connect?
platform.androidBody: Samsung, Pixel, Xiaomi and other Android phones.
platform.iphoneBody: iPhone and iPad. Watch the screen, share files and the clipboard.

method.iosTitle: How do you want to connect your iPhone?
method.iosCable: Recommended. Sharpest picture, the phone's sound, photos, and control from this computer.
method.iosCableMacOnly: Works on a Mac. On this computer, use Wi-Fi with the FreeFlect iPhone app.
method.iosWifi: With the FreeFlect iPhone app. Shares the screen, clipboard and files. Viewing only.
method.title: How do you want to connect?
method.cable: Recommended. The sharpest picture and the easiest setup.
method.wifi: No cable. Needs Android 11 or later and the same Wi-Fi network.

devOptions.title: Turn on Developer options
devOptions.tap: Tap {item} seven times, until it says you are now a developer.
devOptions.help1: Can't find {item}? Search for it with the search bar at the top of Settings.
devOptions.help2: Already see Developer options in Settings? Then this is done, press Continue.
devOptions.help3: Your phone may ask for your PIN or pattern after the taps. That is normal.

usbDebugging.title: Turn on USB debugging
usbDebugging.help1: USB debugging is greyed out? Unplug the cable, turn it on, then plug in again.
usbDebugging.help2: Search Settings for USB debugging if Developer options is somewhere else on your phone.

connect.title: Connect your phone with a USB cable
connect.step2: Plug it into this computer. This page moves on by itself when the phone is found.
connect.fileTransfer: When the phone asks how to use USB, choose File transfer.
connect.help1: Some cables only charge. Try another cable, ideally the one that came with the phone.
connect.help2: Plug straight into the computer instead of a hub or adapter, or try another port.
connect.help3: If the phone asks how to use USB, choose File transfer.

authorize.title: Tap Allow on your phone
authorize.step1: Look for the Allow USB debugging prompt on your phone.
authorize.step2: Tick Always allow from this computer, so you only do this once.
authorize.help1: No prompt? Unlock the phone, then unplug and reconnect the cable.
authorize.help2: Still nothing? In Developer options, tap Revoke USB debugging authorizations, then reconnect.

wifiPair.title: Pair your phone over Wi-Fi
wifiPair.body: Keep your phone and this computer on the same Wi-Fi network.
wifiPair.help1: Wireless debugging turns off when your phone changes networks. Turn it on again.
wifiPair.help2: Pairing keeps failing? Connect with a USB cable once and use Switch to Wi-Fi instead.

iosCable.title: Connect your iPhone with a cable
iosCable.waiting: Plug in the iPhone and unlock it.
iosCable.step1: Unlock your iPhone and plug it into this computer.
iosCable.step2: When the iPhone asks to trust this computer, tap Trust and enter your passcode.
iosCable.step3: Keep the iPhone unlocked. This page moves on by itself when the screen is found.
iosCable.help1: Nothing happens? Unlock the iPhone. Its screen only appears to the computer while it is unlocked.
iosCable.help2: No Trust prompt? Unplug the cable, unlock the iPhone and plug it in again.
iosCable.help3: Tapped Don't Trust by mistake? On the iPhone, open Settings, General, Transfer or Reset iPhone, Reset, Reset Location & Privacy, then reconnect.
iosCable.help4: The first time, FreeFlect explains, then macOS asks to let it use the camera, because it treats the iPhone's screen as one. Allow it. The iPhone's sound stays on the iPhone unless you move it here.

iosApp.title: Install the FreeFlect app on your iPhone
iosApp.body: Connect the iPhone with a cable for this step. This computer builds the app with your own Apple ID or provisioning profile and installs it. Already installed? Press Continue.
iosApp.help1: No teams listed? Open Xcode, Settings, Accounts, and add your Apple ID. A free Apple ID works.
iosApp.help2: Developer Mode is off? On the iPhone, open Settings, Privacy & Security, Developer Mode, and turn it on. The iPhone restarts.
iosApp.help3: The app says it is from an untrusted developer? Open Settings, General, VPN & Device Management, tap the developer, then Trust.
iosApp.help4: With a free Apple ID the app stops opening after 7 days. Install it again from here.

iosPair.title: Pair the iPhone with this computer
iosPair.body: You do this once. After that, only paired iPhones can connect to this computer, and the connection is encrypted.
iosPair.help1: Keep the iPhone and this computer on the same Wi-Fi network. Guest and office networks sometimes block devices from seeing each other.
iosPair.help2: The app says it can't search the network? On the iPhone, open Settings, Privacy & Security, Local Network, and turn on FreeFlect.
iosPair.help3: The code expired or didn't match? Choose Show a new code and try again.

iosBroadcast.title: Share the iPhone's screen
iosBroadcast.waiting: Waiting for the iPhone to start sharing.
iosBroadcast.step1: In the FreeFlect app, tap the round broadcast button. Or open Control Center and touch and hold Screen Recording.
iosBroadcast.help1: FreeFlect is missing from the list? Close and reopen the FreeFlect app, then try again.
iosBroadcast.help2: The broadcast stops right away? Check that the app says connected first.
iosBroadcast.help3: To stop sharing, tap the red status bar at the top of the iPhone, then Stop.

live.foundBody: Waiting for you to tap Allow on the phone.
live.noneUsb: You can plug in your phone at any time.
live.noneWifi: Your phone will appear after pairing.

done.nextTime: Next time it connects by itself.
done.tip1: Click to tap and drag to swipe. Right click goes back.
done.tip2: Type on your keyboard to type on the phone. Cmd or Ctrl+V pastes from this computer.
done.tip3: Drop files on the phone to send them. APK files are installed.

iosDone.nextCable: Next time, plug it in and unlock it.
iosDone.nextWifi: Next time, open the FreeFlect app and start the broadcast.
iosDone.cable1: The iPhone's sound stays on the iPhone. To hear it here, use the Sound on iPhone button.
iosDone.cable2: The folder button shows the iPhone's photos and videos. Drag them out to save them.
iosDone.cable3: Controlling the iPhone from here is a developer feature. It needs Developer Mode on the iPhone and Appium's WebDriverAgent on this Mac.
iosDone.wifi1: Over Wi-Fi the iPhone is view only. Controlling an iPhone needs a cable connection.
iosDone.wifi2: Drop files on the iPhone to send them to the FreeFlect app.
iosDone.wifi3: Use FreeFlect in the iPhone's share sheet to send photos, links and text here.

doctorMain.adbFail: Android connection service is not running
doctorMain.adbFailDetail: {app} uses it to talk to Android phones. Start it and run the checks again.
doctorMain.noPhoneDetail: Use a cable that carries data, not only charging, and try another USB port. If the phone asks how to use USB, choose File transfer.
doctorMain.allowed: This computer is allowed on your phone
doctorMain.notAllowed: Your phone has not allowed this computer yet
doctorMain.notAllowedDetail: Unlock your phone and tap Allow on the USB debugging prompt. If no prompt appears, unplug and reconnect the cable. In Developer options you can also tap Revoke USB debugging authorizations, then reconnect.
doctorMain.notRespondingDetail: Unplug the cable, unlock your phone and plug it back in.
doctorMain.sameNetwork: Phone and computer are on the same network
doctorMain.differentNetworks: Phone and computer seem to be on different networks
doctorMain.differentNetworksDetail: Your phone is at {phone}, this computer at {computer}. Connect both to the same Wi-Fi.
doctorMain.xiaomi: Xiaomi phones also need USB debugging (Security settings) turned on in Developer options, or taps and typing will not reach the phone.
doctorMain.oppo: If taps do not work, turn on Disable permission monitoring in Developer options.
doctorMain.brandOk: No extra settings needed for this brand.
doctorMain.captureFailDetail: Unlock your phone and keep it on, then run the checks again.

ios.macOnly: Mirroring an iPhone over a cable needs a Mac.
ios.helperMissing: The iPhone capture helper is missing from this build
ios.helperMissingDetail: Reinstall FreeFlect. Wi-Fi with the iPhone app still works.
ios.noCableDetail: To mirror over a cable, unlock the iPhone and plug it in. If it asks whether to trust this computer, tap Trust. Using Wi-Fi only? You can ignore this part.
ios.noCableSkip: Needs an iPhone on the cable
ios.yourTerminal: the app you started FreeFlect from
ios.devHolder: FreeFlect is running from {who}, so macOS asks about {who} instead of FreeFlect.
ios.cameraOffDetail: macOS treats the iPhone's screen as a camera. In System Settings, Privacy & Security, Camera, turn on {who}, then quit and reopen {who}.
ios.cameraAsk: macOS hasn't asked for camera access yet
ios.cameraAskDetail: macOS treats the iPhone's screen as a camera and asks once. Choose Ask for access, then Allow.
ios.micOffDetail: The iPhone's sound stays on the iPhone, so that's fine. To hear it on this computer instead, turn on {who} in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Microphone (macOS counts the iPhone's sound as a microphone).
ios.micAskDetail: The iPhone's sound stays on the iPhone. If you move it to this computer, macOS asks about the microphone first, because it counts the iPhone's sound as one.
ios.bothOn: Camera and microphone access are on for {who}
ios.captureFailDetail: Keep the iPhone unlocked and the cable firmly in. If it still fails, unplug the iPhone, plug it in again and run the check again.
ios.offline: This computer isn't on a network
ios.offlineDetail: Connect it to the same Wi-Fi as the iPhone.
ios.firewallAll: The macOS firewall blocks all incoming connections
ios.firewallAllDetail: The iPhone can't reach this computer. In System Settings, Network, Firewall, Options, turn off Block all incoming connections.
ios.firewallAppDetail: In System Settings, Network, Firewall, Options, set {app} to Allow incoming connections.
ios.vpnDetail: Some VPNs stop devices on the same Wi-Fi from reaching each other. If the iPhone can't find this computer, turn the VPN off and try again.
ios.appOff: The iPhone app is turned off on this computer
ios.appOffDetail: Pair an iPhone to turn it on. Nothing listens on the network until then.
ios.notPairedDetail: Pair once with the FreeFlect iPhone app. Only paired iPhones can connect.
ios.notListening: This computer isn't waiting for the iPhone app
ios.notListeningDetail: Quit FreeFlect and open it again. If that doesn't help, copy the report and send it to us.
ios.notAdvertised: The iPhone can't see this computer on the network
ios.notAdvertisedDetail: FreeFlect is waiting, but its announcement on the network didn't go out. Turn Wi-Fi off and on again on this computer, then run the check again.
ios.listening: Waiting for paired iPhones, and visible on the network
ios.noLink: No paired iPhone is connected right now
ios.notSeen: No paired iPhone has connected since FreeFlect started.
ios.noLinkDetail: Open the FreeFlect app on the iPhone, on the same Wi-Fi. If it says this isn't the computer it's paired with, pair it again.

installerMain.addAppleId: Add your Apple ID in Xcode (Settings, Accounts), then try again.

installerMain.unreachable: Xcode can not reach the iPhone. Connect it with a cable, unlock it and try again.
installerMain.buildFailed: The build failed. Open the details for the full log.
installerMain.teamGone: That team is no longer in Xcode. Check Xcode, Settings, Accounts.
installerMain.profile: Getting a signing profile from Apple
installerMain.opening: Opening the app on the iPhone
installerMain.profileGone: That provisioning profile is no longer installed. Press Refresh.
installerMain.profileExpired: The profile "{name}" has expired. Create a new one on developer.apple.com.
installerMain.profileNoDevice: The profile "{name}" doesn't include this iPhone. Add the iPhone to the profile on developer.apple.com, then download it again.

iosControlMain.failed: WebDriverAgent failed to start. It may need to be signed again in Xcode.
iosControlMain.stopped: WebDriverAgent stopped on the iPhone. Turn developer control on again.

iosDevices.needsCable: Connect the iPhone with a cable to {purpose}.
iosDevices.needsCableUnlock: Connect the iPhone with a cable and unlock it to {purpose}.
iosDevices.sameName: Several connected iPhones are called "{name}". Give each one its own name in Settings, General, About, Name.
iosDevices.notFound: Can't tell which connected iPhone this is. Unplug the other iPhones and try again.

wifiMain.expired: The code expired. Close this and try again.
wifiMain.noConnect: Paired, but the phone did not connect. Keep Wireless debugging open and try again.
wifiMain.usePairing: This phone has Wireless debugging. Pair it with the QR code instead, which is encrypted.

camera.title: Show your iPhone's screen
camera.why: To show your iPhone's screen over the cable. macOS hands an iPhone's screen to apps as a camera, so FreeFlect can't show it without camera access.
camera.next: macOS asks whether FreeFlect may use the camera. Choose Allow. If you choose Not now, FreeFlect doesn't ask macOS, and the iPhone isn't shown.
camera.declined: FreeFlect needs camera access to show an iPhone on a cable. Start mirroring again when you're ready.
camera.scope: FreeFlect only opens your iPhone, and only while you mirror it. It never uses this Mac's own camera, and it doesn't record anything unless you press Record.

microphone.title: Play the iPhone's sound on this Mac
microphone.why: To play your iPhone's sound on this Mac, because you asked to. macOS hands an iPhone's sound to apps as a microphone, so FreeFlect can't play it here without microphone access.
microphone.next: macOS asks whether FreeFlect may use the microphone. Choose Allow. If you choose Not now, the sound stays on the iPhone and mirroring works as before.
microphone.declined: The sound stays on the iPhone.
microphone.scope: FreeFlect only opens your iPhone's sound, never this Mac's own microphone. While the iPhone's sound plays here over the cable, macOS shows its microphone indicator (the orange dot), because it counts that sound as a microphone. To turn the indicator off, click Sound on this Mac to keep the sound on the iPhone, or stop mirroring.

pairing.title: Before you pair
pairing.why: Your iPhone reaches this computer over your Wi-Fi to share its screen, clipboard and files. For that, this computer has to be findable on your local network.
pairing.next: macOS may ask whether FreeFlect can find devices on your local network. Choose Allow. If you choose Not now, pairing doesn't start.
pairing.declined: Pairing needs this computer to be reachable on your Wi-Fi. Choose Show a new code when you're ready.
pairing.scope: Only iPhones you pair can connect, and the connection is encrypted. Nothing is reachable on the network until you pair.

keychain.title: FreeFlect needs its keychain item
keychain.why: FreeFlect keeps a key in your keychain that proves this computer to your paired iPhones, so they only share their screen with this Mac. After an update, macOS asks again before FreeFlect can use it.
keychain.next: macOS asks whether FreeFlect may use its keychain item. Choose Always Allow so it doesn't ask again until the next update. If you choose Not now, the iPhone app stays off until you open FreeFlect again; your pairings are kept.
keychain.declined: The iPhone app stays off until FreeFlect can use its keychain item. Open FreeFlect again, or pair the iPhone again, to be asked.
keychain.scope: FreeFlect only reads its own item, “FreeFlect Safe Storage”. It can't see your passwords or other keychain items.
